# Relative R/V photometry of (433) Eros
# Source: DAMIT (Durech, Sidorin & Kaasalainen 2010, A&A 513, A46),
#   https://damit.cuni.cz asteroid id 1714, light curve index 63 of the exportAllForAsteroid plaintext export (retrieved 2026-07-16);
#   original photometry from the literature as archived by DAMIT.
# Ground truth: spacecraft-verified single elongated body (NEAR Shoemaker: 34.4 x 11.2 x 11.2 km, rho = 2.67 g/cm3; Veverka et al. 2000).
# Rotation period: 5.27025528 h (DAMIT).  Spin pole: ecliptic (lambda, beta) = (17, 11) deg.
# Geometry of this block: solar phase angle alpha = 8.8 deg, aspect angle = 84.3 deg (from the DAMIT Sun/Earth vectors).
# The archived block spans 1.12 rotations; its final 18 points
# re-observe already-covered rotational phases but arrive ~8
# minutes (0.025 in phase) early relative to the first coverage
# -- an internal timing inconsistency in the archival composite
# (no plausible period error or synodic effect can produce it
# within a single night).  Only the first full rotation (128
# points) is kept here.
# Differential magnitudes about the block mean (relative photometry;
# a uniform 0.02 mag uncertainty is adopted).
# JD  dmag  err
